text:
emma_sales: Quick sync — Enterprise Z confirmed they want an air-gapped POC. Requirements they listed: minimal offline bundle, delta upgrades (no full redeploy), signed artifacts/SBOM, offline cert rotation, and a short quoted price for a 2-week POC. Can we scope what we can commit to?

diego_se: Short answer: doable. Plan I'd propose: deliver a minibundle that contains the runtime + selected model shards + config manifest. Provide an incremental patch format (chunked tar/rsync-friendly) + signature per-manifest. POC scope: single region, one model variant (quantized), no HSM integration in-phase.

natalie_security: Must have: signed SBOM, manifest with deterministic hashes, instructions for cert rotation offline, and documented patch/RCA cadence for CVEs. Also need to confirm whether customer requires a FIPS-mode runtime build. If so, that's a scope increase.

ash_engineering: Technical constraints to call out:
- We can produce minibundles that only include model shards they want to load to keep size < ~20GB.
- Delta updates: we produce a manifest.json with file entries + byte-range diffs, then sign the manifest with our release key. The client side agent applies diffs locally.
- Offline cert rotation: we support a manual rotation flow: generate CSR on node, hand off to customer CA, import signed cert into keystore. We can write a runbook.

Example manifest snippet (for clarity):
```
{
  "bundle_version": "2024-04-25-1",
  "files": [
    {"path": "runtime/bin/redwood", "sha256": "<hex>", "size": 12583440},
    {"path": "models/vicuna-13b-q4/shard-000", "sha256": "<hex>", "size": 2147483648}
  ],
  "signature": "<base64-sig>"
}
```

diego_se: Packaging command we'd run for POC (example):
```
redwood-pack --model vicuna-13b-q4 --quant q4_0 --include-runtime --sign key.pem --out enterpriseZ-minibundle.tar.gz
redwood-gen-manifest --bundle enterpriseZ-minibundle.tar.gz > manifest.json
sign-manifest --key release.key manifest.json > manifest.json.sig
```

emma_sales: Pricing ask from procurement: one-off POC packaging fee + engineer time + shipping of signed bundles. What ballpark should I give?

ash_engineering: Ballpark: $6k one-time packaging + up to 40h eng support for the 2-week window (we usually estimate $10k for eng hours if they want us on-call), plus $/GPU-month for production. For POC we often grant 30 days of hosted credits if they need compare-to-hosted.

natalie_security: For the security questionnaire answers: I'll need to provide an entry for offline key handling, SBOM generation process, and our patch SLA for critical vulns (we aim for 30 days for infra-critical in customer-managed deploys). If customer demands shorter SLA that changes SOW.

ops-bot: bundle_upload event: enterpriseZ-minibundle.tar.gz uploaded to staging-artifacts at 2024-04-25T15:24:10Z (sha256: abc123...).

emma_sales: Ok — action items: (1) diego/ash create minibundle prototype and run size estimate by EOD Thu, (2) natalie draft security questionnaire answers and offline cert runbook, (3) I'll give procurement the $6k + eng hours estimate and ask about FIPS/HSM requirement.

diego_se: I'll start packing a quantized 13B shard set and report sizes. If we can get them under 25GB it's a much easier network transfer for their site.

natalie_security: FYI: if customer insists on HSM for signing, we can do a manual step where signing happens on their HSM and they provide signed manifests — that removes our ability to re-sign during support. Not ideal for POC.

emma_sales: Thanks everyone. I'll loop in customer for a quick call tomorrow 10am PT to confirm whether they want FIPS/HSM and to agree on a delivery window. :calendar:
